25.08.2021 - L33 and Tinf for CXOU J160103.1-513353, 1WGA J1713.4-3949, and XMMU J172054.5-372652 are updated according to Tables 4, 5, and 7 of Ho et al. (2021). L33 and Tinf are derived from local temperatures and effective emitting areas given in these tables for the carbon atmosphere ("nsx") model fitting. This model is preferred because it gives more plausible effective radii than the other models in the tables, with nearly the same statistical quality. The distances are assumed fixed as per the authors. For 1WGA J1713.4-3949, the data presented by the authors for three observation series (performed in 2001, 2004, and 2014) are averaged, and the uncertainties are enlarged to embrace the uncertainties of all the three sets.

02.11.2022 - updated distance, luminosity, and effective temperature for XMMU J173203.3-344518, following Doroshenko et al. (2022). The effective redshifted temperature Tinf=156±6 eV is derived from the local effective temperature, mass, and local radius (with 1σ uncertainties) for the spectral model carbatm1 (the only model that assumes a uniform temperature) in Table 1 of Doroshenko et al. (2022). From the same table, we estimate L33=10.6+2.1-1.7, 10.8+3.7-3.0, and 10.8±0.8 for models carbatm1, carbatm2, and hatm2, respectively; the second of these estimates is adopted as representative here.
